title: Quotient completeness from the actual left Koszul unit
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $T$, and the left-Koszul functor $C$ and unit $u$ over its completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-sp-power-torsion-limit-models]. Let $M$ be any unbounded strict complex and suppose $u_M:M\to C(M)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. There exist a flat-term K-flat complex $P$, a quasi-isomorphism $f:P\to M$, its localization isomorphism $e_P:Q(P)\cong Q(M)$ with hom Q(f), and an isomorphism $s:Q(C(M))\cong Q(\mathsf R_j(P\otimes_R (O/\pi^{j+1})_T))$ in the actual scalar-extension-and-restriction model [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. They obey $Q(u_M)s=e_P^{-1}Q(\mathrm{roosUnit}_P)$ and, after every unshifted quotient projection, $Q(u_M)s Q(\mathrm{ev}_j)=e_P^{-1}Q(\mathrm{augmentation}_{P,j})$. The actual derived quotient tower has a product and a distinguished Roos triangle with first object Q(M), first-map components $e_P^{-1}Q(\mathrm{augmentation}_{P,j})$, and second map one minus shift. Finally Q(M) is derived complete in the unrestricted integral coefficient convention [def-weil-derived-complete], equivalently IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete at the none slice. No strict outer tower or nilpotence hypothesis occurs here.

source.place: Completeness sentence, principal Koszul calculation and canonical quotient projections; Bhatt--Scholze, Lemmas 3.4.12 and 3.5.4--3.5.7.

proof.text: Completed uniformizer multiplication is regular and its power quotients are the actual finite coefficient sheaves. Choose one flat-term K-flat resolution f:P to M. Apply the strict Koszul/quotient bridge with this P and the normalized ordinary scalar-extension presentation; both span maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Identify localization with Q using quotientCompQhIso and the two strict Roos models by their identical product cone maps. The span gives s and both displayed normalization equations.

proof.text: Since u_M is a quasi-isomorphism, kappa=e_P inverse followed by Q(roosUnit_P) is invertible. The strict quotient tower has its distinguished Roos triangle. Transport its first object through kappa: replace its first map a by kappa a and its connecting morphism d by d followed by the shifted inverse of kappa. Projection to j gives the already identified canonical quotient component. The middle arrow stays one minus shift.

source.place: Completeness sentence, principal Koszul calculation and canonical quotient projections; Bhatt--Scholze, Lemmas 3.4.12 and 3.5.4--3.5.7.

proof.text: For the none slice, the scalar-extension tower on P equals the legacy integral reduction tower on that same P, and its augmentation equals the legacy unit. Choose a finite auxiliary field of characteristic distinct from ell; the completed coefficient sheaf is independent of this auxiliary choice. The preceding transported triangle with this resolution is the witness required by IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted, which defines IsComplete at none.

lean.statement:
theorem left_koszul_quotient_completeness
    (M : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E T) ℤ)
    (hu : QuasiIso (unit l E T M)) :
        ∃ (P : (IntegralOnSlice.Good l E T none).FullSubcategory)
          (f : P.obj ⟶ M)
          (eP : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)
          (s : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((completion l E T).obj M) ≅
            DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((roos l E T).obj
              ((IntegralOnSlice.tower l E T none).obj P.obj))),
          QuasiIso f ∧ eP.hom = DerivedCategory.Q.map f ∧
          DerivedCategory.Q.map (unit l E T M) ≫ s.hom =
            eP.inv ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (IntegralOnSlice.roosUnit l E T none P.obj) ∧
          (∀ j : ℕ,
            DerivedCategory.Q.map (unit l E T M) ≫ s.hom ≫
                DerivedCategory.Q.map (evaluation l E T
                  ((IntegralOnSlice.tower l E T none).obj P.obj) j) =
              eP.inv ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map
                (((IntegralOnSlice.augmentation l E T none).app P.obj).app (op j))) ∧
          (∃ (hprod : HasProduct (fun j : ℕ ↦
                (IntegralOnSlice.derivedTower l E T none P).obj (op j))),
            (fun [_hp : HasProduct (fun j : ℕ ↦
                (IntegralOnSlice.derivedTower l E T none P).obj (op j))] ↦
            ∃ (p : DerivedCategory.Q.obj M ⟶
                ∏ᶜ fun j : ℕ ↦ (IntegralOnSlice.derivedTower l E T none P).obj (op j))
            (δ : (∏ᶜ fun j : ℕ ↦
                (IntegralOnSlice.derivedTower l E T none P).obj (op j)) ⟶
              (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
            IsDerivedLimitTriangle
              (fun j : ℕ ↦ (IntegralOnSlice.derivedTower l E T none P).map
                (homOfLE j.le_succ).op) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) p δ ∧
            ∀ j : ℕ, p ≫ Pi.π _ j = eP.inv ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map
              (((IntegralOnSlice.augmentation l E T none).app P.obj).app (op j)))
              (_hp := hprod)) ∧
          IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E T none
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)
